findings.evidence: `pkg/ddl/job_scheduler.go`: `ownerListener.OnBecomeOwner()` sets `reorgCtx` owner stamp via `time.Now().Unix()` (second granularity). `pkg/ddl/reorg.go`: `runReorgJob()` tags `reorgFnResult.ownerTS` with `beOwnerTS := w.ddlCtx.reorgCtx.getOwnerTS()` and only treats results as stale when `res.ownerTS != curTS`. `pkg/owner/manager.go`: `campaignLoop()` can call `toBeOwner()` again immediately after `RetireOwner()` with no enforced delay, so multiple `OnBecomeOwner()` calls can occur within the same second. `upstream/master` still uses `time.Now().Unix()` for this stamp.
findings.fix: Use a monotonic owner-epoch instead of wall-clock seconds: e.g. store `ownerEpoch` as an `atomic.Int64` (or `atomicutil.Int64`) incremented on every `OnBecomeOwner()`, and record/compare that epoch in `reorgFnResult`. If wall time is preferred, at least switch to `time.Now().UnixNano()` plus a fallback atomic counter to guarantee uniqueness.
findings.impact: If the instance loses and regains DDL ownership within the same second, `ownerTS` can collide and stale `reorgFn` completion (often driven by canceled scheduler context / ownership change) can be misclassified as current, reintroducing the original owner-change bug (potentially causing incorrect DDL failure/rollback or incorrect state-machine progression).
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (f0813a3696): the stamp/compare mechanism remains and still uses `time.Now().Unix()` in `pkg/ddl/job_scheduler.go`.
findings.verify: Force rapid owner re-election (e.g. via owner-manager failpoints / resign loop) so `OnBecomeOwner()` runs twice within one second while a reorg goroutine completes; confirm current code can accept the stale result when the stamp collides, and confirm the proposed epoch-based fix always treats the old result as stale regardless of timing.
findings.what: Owner-generation stamp uses `time.Now().Unix()` (seconds), so rapid owner re-elections can reuse the same `ownerTS`, defeating the stale-result filter in `runReorgJob()`.

subject: ddl: record get owner TS and compare it before runReorgJob quit (#55049)
summary: The change correctly tags reorg goroutine results with an owner stamp to ignore stale completions across DDL owner changes, but the chosen stamp (`time.Now().Unix()` seconds) is not a unique owner-epoch and can collide under rapid re-elections, allowing stale results through.
